sources.citation: Cárdenas A., Renato, Dante Montiel Vera & Catherine Grace Hall. 1991. Los chono y los veliche de Chiloé. Santiago de Chile: Olimpho. sources.note: Nothing on the sound system of the Calen/Taijataf language. The only prosodic remarks in the book are Emperaire's impressions of (Puerto Eden) Alacaluf speech and song quoted on pp. 87-88 ('guturales muy atenuadas.. una especie de canto en voz baja'; songs 'se caracterizan por una acentuacion muy fuerte de las silabas, todas bien cortadas') -- about Kawesqar performance style, not word stress, and not this languoid -- and a footnote on the final accent of the ethnonym 'caucahue' as a possible Mapudungun influence on colonial writers.

Washington: Government Printing Office. Pp. 31-32, 38-40 (Calens and Taijatafes/Tayatafar; linguistic affiliation of the canoe peoples south of the Gulf of Peñas).
sources.note: No phonology. Translates García Martí/Hervás: 'The Calen and Taijataf nations speak the same language, which is quite guttural and not at all like Araucanian; the two nations can understand each the other's language, though it appears that each has its own dialect' (p. 39), and argues García 'would have had an opportunity.. to pick up a few phrases at least of their language(s)' but recorded none. Nothing on stress, accent or tone.
